headline: The American Academy of Pediatrics told pediatricians how generative AI should and should not be used on children.
score_reason: First formal guidance from the main US pediatric body, official and dated, but a policy statement rather than a binding rule.
importance_line: Children treated with AI-assisted tools gain a stated standard for privacy, oversight and child-specific design; hospitals and developers now have a benchmark, though the AAP cannot enforce it and admits the evidence is still catching up with adoption.
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics said on 3 Oct 2026 that it has published a policy statement, out in the November 2026 issue of Pediatrics, on using generative AI in children's clinical care, calling for tools built for children rather than adapted from adult models, strong privacy safeguards, bias checks and "rigorous human oversight and accountability", in the words of lead author Srinivasan Suresh. The group notes that most such tools are trained on data in which children are underrepresented and few have been properly tested in pediatrics; the statement covers clinicians' use only, with separate guidance for families still in preparation.
notes: Text read is the AAP's own press release as carried by Mirage News, so the credit goes to the AAP; no aap.org link was available in the text.
